Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 44 s. 2023 JUN 20 2023 MR. CARLITO DIAZ Proprietor Carljoy Bldg., Juan Luna St., Bogo City, Cebu, Philippines Dear Mr. Diaz: This has reference to your letter dated March 15, 2023 seeking legal opinion from this Department on the following issues: I. Which government agency can certify and enforce an ordinance that is considered "deemed approved"? Is it the government of Medelin or the Cebu Provincial Board? 2. In the absence of certification that said ordinance regarding reclassification is "deemed approved", is the Department of Agrarian Reform (DAR) and other government agencies can bind itself to the opinion of the DILG on the matter? per your representation, you purchased an agricultural land in the Municipality of Medellin, Cebu for residential and other possible uses. The said lot was purchased from an agrarian reform beneficiary and thus, you applied for DAR conversion clearance. You also stated that the agricultural land was reclassified by the Municipality of Medellin into mixed-use thru Municipal Ordinance No. 381-2019 which was passed in December 2019. However, the said ordinance was not acted upon by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Cebu up to now. Hence, your request for legal opinion. To clarify the context of herein request, we can discern from the representations that Municipal Ordinance No. 381-2019 of the Municipality of Medellin, Cebu has been duly passed by the sangguniang bayan and approved by the municipal mayor thereat. Pursuant to Section 56 (a) of RA 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991, the approved ordinance was forwarded to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Cebu for "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

review. However, since then up to the date of your letter, the SP of Cebu has not exercised its review power over Municipal Ordinance No. 381-2019 (either approved or disapproved). In answering your queries, we deemed it wise to explain first the distinction between terms "effectivity" and "validity" as mentioned and used under the Local Government code of 1991 (RA 7160). Effectivity is the time by which an ordinance is made effective and can already be implemented and given full force and effect. Effectivity is governed by Section 59(a) of the Local Government Code of 1991 , thus: SECTION 59. Effectivity of Ordinances or Resolutions. (a) Unless otherwise stated in the ordinance or the resolution approving the local development plan and public investment program, the same shall take effect after ten (10) days from the date a copy thereof is posted in a bulletin board at the entrance of the provincial capitol or city, municipal, or Barangay hall, as the case may be, and in at least two (2) other conspicuous places in the local government unit concerned. xxxx Based on the foregoing, an ordinance of a local government unit becomes effective as of the date the framers of such ordinance would like it to be effective and in the absence of such effectivity clause, the same shall take effect after ten (10) days from the date a copy thereof is posted in a bulletin board at the entrance of the municipal hall and in at least two (2) other conspicuous places in the local government unit concerned. Thus, upon approval thereof by the Municipal Mayor and after compliance with the posting requirement, the Municipal Ordinance shall, as a matter of course, be already given legal effect and implemented even if the same is still pending review by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. Validity, on the other hand, refers to the substantive requirement of an ordinance, whether the same is consistent with the Constitution and laws. When the Sangguniang Panlalawigan reviews a Municipal Ordinance pursuant to Section 56 of the Local Government Code of 1991, which we quote herein for reference: "Section 56. Review of Component City and Municipal Ordinances or Resolutions by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan.-- (a) Within three (3) days after approval, the secretary to the sanggunian panlungsod or sangguniang bayan shall forward to the sangguniang panlalawigan for review, copies of approved ordinances and the resolutions approving the local development plans and public investment programs formulated by the local development councils. (b) Within thirty (30) days after the receipt of copies of such ordinances and resolutions, the sangguniang panlalawigan shall examine the documents or transmit them to the provincial attorney, or if there be none, to the provincial prosecutor for prompt examination. The provincial attorney or provincial prosecutor shall, within a period of ten (10) days from receipt of the Page 2 of 4

(b) For efficient, effective and economical governance the purpose of which is the general welfare of the municipality and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code, the municipal mayor shall: Xxxx (2) Enforce all laws and ordinances relative to the qovernance of the municipality and the exercise of its corporate powers provided for under Section 22 of this Code implement all approved policies, programs, projects, services and activities of the municipality Xxxx (emphasis supplied) From the foregoing, the Municipal Mayor is responsible for enforcing all laws and ordinances pertaining to municipal governance, the goal of which is the general welfare of the municipality and its inhabitants. Since the subject ordinance is a Municipal Ordinance, the Municipal Mayor of Medellin should enforce and implement the ordinance. As to the second query. our courts are not bound by the legal opinions rendered by the Department. However, jurisprudence is replete of cases saying that DILG Legal Opinions are nevertheless accorded persuasive effect on issues involving Republic Act No. 7160, or the Code. The DILG legal opinions, in proper cases, can also be a source of good faith on the part of the public official who acted based thereon or bad faith on those who acted contrary thereto. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. It is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you.
